overview: Regulatory Submission Evidence Assembly addresses source evidence is scattered across documents and transaction systems, leading to repeated checks and incomplete case files in pharma and life sciences operations. The first proof of value uses CTD modules, approvals and controlled SOP versions. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is submission deficiencies found before filing, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: CTD modules, approvals and controlled SOP versions; define submission deficiencies found before filing and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of Quality / Clinical Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including run golden documents and exceptions against the system of record.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
